historical_references.reference: According to Arthurian legend, Shauron was a sorceress and the mother of Mordred, King Arthur's illegitimate son. She was said to have bewitched Merlin and helped Mordred to defeat King Arthur in the Battle of Camlann. This legend likely developed during the High Middle Ages, around the 12th century.

In Christian folklore, Shauron (or Saron) is a demon or evil spirit associated with the sea. She is sometimes equated with the Greek goddess Tyche or the Roman goddess Fortuna, and is believed to have the power to cause storms and shipwrecks. This belief may have originated in the early Christian period, around the 4th or 5th century.
